methods.scaling_rule: required = minimum x team games played / 82
methods.scaling_text: Each minimum is a full-season (82-game) bar set by the owner after reviewing the reliability study's curves; the study did not choose them. The bar scales with the team games played by the player's current team: required = minimum x team games played / 82. For example, after 41 team games the free throw % bar is 125 attempts.
methods.traded_players: A traded player's sample counts every game he played this season, for any team, and is held to the bar of the team he played for most recently.
methods.position_note: Positions are the box-score listing, and some players are listed broadly (for example "F"). A combined listing such as "G-F" counts under its first letter.
methods.ranking: Ranked by per-game average, percentage or rate. For turnovers and turnover rate the lowest figure leads. Ties share a rank.
methods.noise_note: The 3-point %, effective field goal %, true shooting % and RAPM cards are mostly noise at season sample sizes (split-half reliability at the chosen minimums: 3P% about 0.26; eFG% and TS% about 0.63; total RAPM about 0.59).

rate_formulas.usg_pct: 100 x ((FGA + 0.44 x FTA + TOV) x (TmMP / 5)) / (MP x (TmFGA + 0.44 x TmFTA + TmTOV))
rate_formulas.summing: Summed over the player's games: value = sum of numerators / sum of denominators. TmMP is the sum of the team's player minutes in that game.

methods.refresh: Box-score and rate cards update in the 09:00 pipeline run and in the evening score refreshes. RAPM cards update in the 09:00 run only. Each card shows its own through date.
methods.sample: Regular-season games only. A game counts when the player is not listed as did-not-play and has minutes recorded.
methods.nulls: Values that cannot be supported are null with a reason; nothing is imputed or synthesised.

season_totals.description: Per-player season sums behind the box-score cards (numerators, denominators and samples), team games played and the game ids included, so the evening refresh can add new games.
